items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: "Fish Market Blues" with Roy Eldridge, that record.

ctx.x: Yeah. It's funny, you know, how -- I often tell pupils this kind of thing and they'll put down other musicians. They don't want to work in a band, this musician's bad. So I sort of sound like Will Rogers, but it's the truth, I've never met a trumpet player who can't do something I can't do, you know. And not one of those guys who can do something I can't do is not perfectly happy to tell you exactly what it is, you know. And you can learn a hell of a lot. Instead of putting down the guy sitting next to you,…

I'd go up to there place in the morning or something. Roy used to live -- I think it was Edgecombe Avenue. He had a pot full of chili, which I think he lived on. I don't think he ever ate anything but chili, morning, noon and night. And he would start practicing about 10:00 in the morning and he would just start in on a piece. And he would just play this piece everyway he could. Not that he worked his solos out, but he would just play and --

items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: This is after I made "Rockin' Chair." It featured Jimmy Maxwell. He's a great trumpet player

ctx.x: If anybody was going to take a ballad on that thing, it should have been me, right? This is after I made "Rockin' Chair." It featured Jimmy Maxwell. He's a great trumpet player, but I mean, I think I should have done the ballad. But they featured him. And it was just like a... Well, it was just the wrong thing, man, you know. It was just like having a .400 hitter and you keep him on the bench.

And see, they never once had to stop for me to read the music, like what they did for those cats. That's another thing. I remember it took them quite some time to get through with that arrangement, you know. The only time they started with me at first was when they first ...(?)..., and he asked me to take a look at it. And I looked at it and I said, "Is it in one?" He said, "No." He said, "Well, take a look." I said, "Well, I'm looking. Is this the wrong key signature or what?" It was (?). It started out as a…

items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: E ie Royal was an exception because he was a great high note player and they always had to have him because he was the best around on that.

ctx.x: The only thing was that studio -- the studio worked just like everybody else, they had categories. And I know that if you were a black musician you were a jazz player and you didn't get too much calls to be a lead player. E ie Royal was an exception because he was a great high note player and they always had to have him because he was the best around on that. But it worked both ways. If they were going to have a white guy who played perfectly good jazz and maybe not very good lead, they would call in a black guy…
